title: US consumer prices likely snapped back after being restrained by government shutdown distortions
load_bearing_forecast_sentence: The CPI likely increased by 0.3% last month amid higher food and energy prices, mostly electricity because of data centers, a Reuters survey of economists predicted.
core_forecast_sentence: Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the CPI is forecast to have increased 0.3% in December.
yoy_forecast_sentence: In the 12 months through December, the CPI is forecast to have increased 2.7%, matching November's gain. / The so-called core CPI was predicted to have advanced 2.7% year-on-year in December after gaining 2.6% in November.
shutdown_context_sentence: The BLS estimated the CPI rose 0.2% from September to November. The carry-forward imputation method treated October prices as unchanged.
target_disambiguation: headline MoM = 0.3% (unqualified 'The CPI'); core MoM = 0.3% (explicitly 'excluding the volatile food and energy components'); headline YoY = 2.7%; core YoY = 2.7%. Headline/core MoM coincide numerically but are stated in separate, distinctly-labeled sentences.
